Ad5-mediated gene transfer of wild-type DTT can sensitize tumor cells that are resistant to the chemotherapeutic agent MMC and that this strategy can be effective in the absence of bystander effects.

(i) Ad5-mediated delivery of wild-type DDTD to mutant DTD-expressing BE cells sensitizes these cells to the cytotoxic effects of MMC; and (ii) the sensitization of BE cells is due to increased DTD activity and is accompanied by an increased sensitivity to the cytotoxic effect of MMC.

Ad5-mediated expression of wild-type, but not mutant, DTD can sensitizer human colon carcinoma cells that are deficient in DTD to MMC and that the sensitization effect is due, at least in part, to bystander killing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a gene therapy approach to treat cancer by the use of recombinant viruses to deliver a prodrug-activizing enzyme to tumor cells.
the use of adenoviral vectors as vehicles for delivering genes encoding enzymes that activate prodrugs to tumor cells.

the development of a novel approach for the treatment of solid tumors, which involves intratumoral administration of recombinant Ad vectors carrying prodrug-activizing genes, such as DTD, and subsequent administration of the appropriate prodrug.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
adenovirus mediated gene therapy for the treatment of cancer is a viable and potentially powerful approach to cancer therapy.
Ad5-mediated delivery of DTD to tumor cells is a promising approach to the treatment of human tumors.
Ad5-mediated gene therapy can be a useful tool in the treatment of cancer.
